All 374 catch taxa have an assigned group: 100% of 2019 landings and simple-chain PPR are mapped. Unresolved taxa: none. This includes 10 Very low assignments covering 12.2032% of landings and 4.0110% of simple-chain PPR; their taxa, weights and reasons are flagged in the Excel appendix.

Catch composition is unknown; compatible named and residual pools provide a broad approximation. Exact candidates and assumptions are in the appendix.

The historical opah label represents offshore deep-living fishes and a subsequently divided species complex. The adopted shelf large-pelagic pair remains a closest represented analogue without an established link to the source guild's sampled assemblage.

Escolar is principally a continental-slope fish below 200 m with upward night movements. The adopted shelf large-pelagic pair remains a weak analogue; a competing benthopelagic interpretation and the missing deep-water compartment are unresolved.

Whole model-pool catch proportions are assumed representative of regional taxon catches across 1950–2019 and all catch bases. These are not observed target-catch mixtures. Another 57 taxa retain Low confidence because of size, habitat or source-group ambiguity.

The four residual fish labels follow verified bony-fish reporting scope; dedicated demersal and pelagic shark/ray pools are excluded. Unknown composition and whole-region transfer remain Very low; complete source catch supplies Medium allocation weights.
